intro.title: useLocalStorage
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses the browser's localStorage to save and retrieve a user's name. You will learn how to create a reactive form to capture input and manage state with Angular's built-in features. The core concept involves persisting data across browser sessions using the Web Storage API. You'll work with TypeScript for type safety, Angular templates for the UI, and lifecycle hooks to initialize the stored value.
intro.usecase: The useLocalStorage pattern is essential for creating seamless user experiences in real-world Angular applications. You'll implement this when building shopping carts that persist items between sessions, user preference panels that remember theme or layout choices, and form wizards that save progress if users navigate away. Product dashboards use localStorage to maintain filter selections and column visibility, while authentication flows often store tokens or session data temporarily. This pattern prevents data loss and creates more responsive interfaces by keeping state client-side.
